item.title: Ms. G. Lass
item.description: Glass lady is smoking hot. Literally.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXX has no bodily orifices and all their skin is replaced with glass. The rest of them is hollow. They were created in a glass factory explosion in Toulouse, France. They were formerly known as Georgine Lass. They were the only survivor. They have a strong hatred for transparent objects due to this, and will attempt to crack, break, or otherwise damage them when in line of sight. When exposed to even a very small amount of oxygen, they will engulf in flames reaching a temperature of 4000K. When this happens, they begin to run around erratically, usually burning though everything and everyone it comes close too.

Central Narrative: Due to the severe flammability, all methods that foundation has thus far have been found not heat resistant enough, hence ineffective. It follows the logs of a pair of containment engineers working, getting pressured, mishaps, everything, as they try to create a containment chamber capable of containing them as they posed a severe containment risk and breached containment several times. They eventually do succeed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be 2 versions of the file, 1 before the success, and 1 after. The before one will have an O5 notice stating “All Containment Engineer Personal at Site X, unless told otherwise by a Foundation Employee with Level 4 Clearance or above, must focus all research, time, and resources to the creation of a containment chamber for SCP-XXX. The budget for containment has been increased to [Large Amount Of Site’s Local Currency].”

Additional Notes: It's not just containment breaches 24/7, but more 1 monthly give or take. I will also have a recontainment procedure so it's not like it takes days to recontain.

item.title: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.description: Hi. After studying the site for a while I've written up my first idea for an SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional and symbolic, with undertones of mystery and light comedic moments

Page Layout: Traditional, with an account of the recovery, and addendum containing testing logs, and a few interviews.

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious black, metal object resembling an hourglass appears in the sky above a foundation site and crashes through the roof. The object appears to consume the time of living beings near it, causing them to leap forward in time and age accordingly. The object ends up killing several researchers, but one seems to be unaffected. The object later even goes as far as to attach itself to him. This researcher then has to grapple with survivor's guilt, and must learn to keep moving forward, accepting both the good and the bad of the object being attached to him.

+ Additional Details
- Additional Details

Central Narrative: (Ultimately, I want to tell a human story about a man initially struggling with guilt, but with the help of a friend, is able to accept the way things are and work to move forward.) After crashing into a foundation site, the SCP lands near a researcher. The anomaly then proceeds to scan him. After the anomaly is contained, the research wants to learn more about it, and is appointed head researcher. During a routine examination, the SCP activates, while our main researcher and two others are in the room. The two other researchers are killed by the SCP, but our main researcher is left. Later, the SCP permanently attaches itself to him. Through interviews with Dr. Glass, we learn he is suffering with survivor’s guilt and isolation. During subsequent testing, we find out that the SCP can allow the researcher to exist outside of time. (Time stop) The end of the arc will have the researcher coming to terms with the conflict he feels towards the SCP being attached to him and using it to help the foundation/the world, while leaving the origin and purpose of the SCP open ended.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: In addition to a relatable human struggle, throughout the article, there’s hints here and there that the SCP may have been intentionally created by an unknown group.

Additional Notes: I’m hoping to expand on the backstory of the SCP in future tales or articles, as well as feature the researcher in some of my future articles. While I couldn’t explain every detail here, I have the main arc of the story pretty well thought out. Critique and greenlights welcome.

item.title: Admin Panel
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (with ACS)

Genre (Optional ): Science-Fiction

Page Layout (Optional ): Classic SCP styling with logs on how far down researchers have dug into the program.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is essentially the admin panel of the local universe, for example, the ability to explore the universe in a single program along with "editing", usually being extremely sophisticated (To the Planck scale)

Addtional details
Hide

Central Narrative: After a world-wide phenomenon wherein the gravity of Earth significantly increased, the foundation investigated the "source" of the phenomenon rumored to be at an abandoned facility, locals claiming that said facility suddenly appeared 2 days ago. The facility was empty, but investigators found a computer alien to Human-made devices. Upon opening the computer, it was found to contain only one program, named "בְּרִיאָה IIV", translated from Hebrew: "Creation".

After bringing the computer to a foundation site, the program was put into testing, showing a 3-d map of the universe, with the ability to "edit" certain aspects of it. The map can be fast-forwarded. Upon selecting earth, it has been seen that gravity was set to "1.0294 G", assumed to be an imperfection after the gravity change 2 days prior. After setting gravity to exactly 1, people reported "feeling some sort of lesser weight", with it reported to be extremely mild.

After scrolling down ~5 meters, investigators noticed that the program has the ability to manipulate the amount of intelligence a species has. The "Cognitive Factor" for humans was set to 0.00109, apes having their CF being at 0.0084. Investigators set the CF of "Canis lupus familiaris" (dogs) at 0.0079 from the value 0.00204. 2 weeks later, a dog was reported to be able to communicate in morse after a researcher decided to teach a dog international morse code, stating that it was to test if said program worked after hearing of the incident and the dog intelligence change.

Lastly, a notable ability of the program is to change the laws of physics themselves. Formulas of every aspect of physics are editable, known or unknown, including gravity, laws of motion, etc.
The SCP can edit and create, such as astronomical phenomena, time, and the very foundations of physics, all branches of it.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The SCP is God's Program. Stolen, tweaked, then contained.

Additional Notes: Would be nice to get tips for a lot more features.

item.title: The Hinterland Division (How many apocalypses could there be?)
item.description: Can you, a normal foundation agent who has just been promoted, save humanity? If so... how many times and at what cost?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale, Site Dossier, Other (It is a combination of all the previous ones using a hub page)

Elevator Pitch: The O5 council creates a new staff classification with O5 security clearance that works under direct orders of the O5 to allow them to have more staff at their disposal for operations that couldn't be told about to those with a lower security level. An agent at the Foundation is promoted to this new staff designation and is assigned to watch over an O5 level security project designed to stop end of the world scenarios from happening.

Central Narrative: In light of several new SCP discoveries that could lead to end of the world scenarios the O5 council decides that methods need to be made for dealing with problems like these, so they make a new project and promote the most reliable agent they have to a recently made position which grants him O5 level clearance. He’s assigned to spearhead the project, creating his own team and coming up with methods to then test and hopefully find the best method to deal with every SCP object or threat, reporting everything he’s doing directly to the council. There will be SCP’s referenced and it will also include several that I’m coming up with. As the agent continues coming up with new methods he starts compiling journals of those involved in the testing of those methods as well as the journals of those who were under the effects by the objects before the methods were tested, revealing to him how much sacrifice they will have to make and have been making to move forward.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that the incorporation of an character who is overseeing the files being the one who you are in the perspective of is pretty unique and different from other things on the site as they mostly don’t give the reader a character.

Additional Notes: I have not nearly finished yet so I won't be posting the sandbox pages very soon as there is still a lot to figure out in terms of the story. I just want to know if the concept is good enough that I should continue it and I want to get greenlit earlier on so I don’t have to worry about it later, I’m not sure if this will need to be split into several drafts since the pages will inevitably have cross links to each other in them

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 15 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Effect is purely proximity-based – object safely observable from a distance. 3 – 72 hours after hallucinations begin, these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made several times to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: As this is my first SCP idea I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away!

item.title: Greenlight: Healing SCP with potential for GK scenario
item.description: Scp I drafted up before reading about the Greenlight process
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: 250 year old clockwork Mannequin SCP with anomalous healing properties that searches for injured humans within a large, exponentially increasing range and attempts to heal them through anomalous means. The range of its search doubles every 4 hours that it doesn't have someone to heal and it gets more and more agitated that it can't find someone to heal. After 24 hours it will attempt to heal terminal medical conditions, resulting in accidental euthanasia. Theorised that if the range encompasses the entire globe, the earth itself may be 'healed' of humanity.

Central Narrative: SCP is picked up through word of mouth rumour and is reported to the coucil who send an mtf team after it. MTF epsilon 6 apprehend the SCP in sweeden, where the locals attempt to stop the task force from attacking it and try to persuade them it just wants to help. MTF team retrieve the SCP which begins becoming aggressive as it cannot reach the subject it wanted to heal. Once it's taken back to a foundation site, it's placed under low level containment during testing of properties as it didn't break initial mtf containment. After a task force operation results in an operator falling into a critical condition, the SCP breaks containment, incapacitating but not wounding security team members that attempt to stop it, and goes to protect the fatally wounded mtf operator until the doctors approach calmly and it let's them help. After this its moved to special containment and special procedures are put in place.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: large initial range of detection with exponentially increasing range as time passes and the SCP goes without healing someone. To help contain it, injured class D personnel are given to the entity heal to stop it from causing a potential humanity extinction event.

Additional Notes: the severity of the injury also increases the aggression level of the SCP

item.title: Hospital that heals you on its own.

A hospital that heals any injured or sick humans that enter, and tries it with other life and artificial items too, with mixed results.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A hospital, in a relatively populated area. Anyone who is sick, or injured, that walks in, will start to recover or heal, across the course of a few days to a few months, depending. Non-human life mutates, as if it's trying to become human, and ends up dead. Broken or damaged artificial objects 'heal' over with human biological components. 'Nurse' entities appear as body disposal, and to move immobile 'patients' to a bed. Where they come from is unknown, but they don't heal, they just don't die.

Central Narrative: On the worldbuilding side, this'll be in a relatively populated area, and may require not only fancy containment procedures, due to the hospital keeping itself looking in working order, and sending out "appointment" letters to the local area, somehow aware of illness or injury within a certain radius of it. Given its location, it may also require cooperation with a GoI, or local authorities, or some sort of group outside of the foundation. Perhaps it got discovered by two at a roughly similar time, or otherwise the foundation had it first, but then some other group (likely the GOC given they are, to my knowledge, the most able to show their faces in public, or the UIU if I put this in the states) turns up.

+ show block
– hide block

Experiment wise, it'll probably be a case of them trying to see how far it'll go, finding it can cure anomalous diseases (if the patient is still alive and human), and injuries, as well as things not thought fixable by modern medicine. item.content:encoded:

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a (now neutralized) spatial anomaly in the outer-reaches of the solar system in the form of an Einstein–Rosen bridge (aka wormhole). On the other side, they can detect a planet. Emission spectroscopy implies that the planet may be habitable. Foundation personnel are sent through, and subsequent events shake the Foundation's view of what they think they know.

+ Additional details
- Additional details

Central Narrative: After probes fail to return from the wormhole, the Foundation sends a manned mission through the wormhole in hopes of finding a new habitable world. The narrative follows them in the form of a series of mission logs. When they arrive on the other side, they are unable to communicate with Command. They find themselves around a rocky planet, not dissimilar to our own.

One of the crew gets in the lander to land on the planet and assess the habitability. Meanwhile, those that remained on the mothership perform scans of the solar system to check for other orbital bodies. The crew come to an astonishing revelation, the solar system doesn't look much different to our own. That's when they realise the wormhole didn't send them through space, it sent them through time. Approximately 4 billion years into the past. The ground crew landed on a primordial Earth, which they've now seeded with nucleotides, nucleases, bacteria etc. The wormhole starts to become unstable and so the crew in orbit make the difficult decision to make their way back to the wormhole. It was in vain, however, as the wormhole closes and they are left in a highly elliptical orbit around the sun, completely out of fuel. Modern day Foundation find the ancient spacecraft, and the final log of the captain, detailing on how he believes they kickstarted abiogenesis (life from non-life).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Humanity inadvertently jump started life on Earth by landing on the primordial Earth 4 billion years in the past. Our unknowing astronauts mediated abiogenesis - life from non-life. All of Earth's life can be traced back to a single common ancestor, created through the highly unlikely and poorly understood event of abiogenesis. This event.

Additional Notes: Any tips on how to tighten the plot would be great.

It can phase through everything that isn't living flesh (e.g. LIVING animals, LIVING humans), but this ability is nullified if its temperature is lowered below -50 degrees Celsius, or 223 degrees Kelvin.

+ show block
– hide block

Once in containment, SCP-XXXX does not require any sort of furniture in its containment cell (made of mirror-like reflective metal to ensure its presence), only needing a cooling system to keep it from phasing out of the room. It does need to be fed, and its meals consist of wild animals and, if a test takes an unfortunate turn, an unlucky Class-D personnel.

It acts like an aggressive and predatory animal despite its humanoid form, and will attack anything, including other SCPs. It will claw at the walls of its cell, and if it breaks the cooling system, it can breach containment. This aggression is seemingly nullified while SCP-XXXX is in the presence of SCP-XXXX-B.

SCP-XXXX-B is the infant born from SCP-XXXX. It resembles a humanoid infant with lighter colored skin than its parent. It shares the same invisibility as its parent, but has not yet displayed any signs of aggression.

Central Narrative: The details of SCP-XXXX's containment are yet undisclosed, but many researchers in the Foundation have suggested that it be reclassified to Thaumiel due to its aforementioned aggression. While the subject is still up for debate, its classification remains Keter, due to its extreme aggression and repeated attempts at breaching containment.

At some point, some people suggested that SCP-XXXX could be the last piece in the puzzle that is the destruction of SCP-682, but due to the incredibly high likelihood of failure, the possibility has been dropped completely.

In the months following the containment of SCP-XXXX, it is discovered to have been pregnant, and it gives birth to SCP-XXXX-B while in containment. This, followed by repeated sightings of SCP-XXXX out in the wild despite it being in containment confirms that SCP-XXXX is not an isolated anomaly, but an entire species of creatures with the same abilities.

item.content:encoded:

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation finds hundreds of dead whales in the middle of the woods, with no idea how they got there. Turns out to be foul play.

Central Narrative: On an otherwise idyllic day in a sleepy small town in British Columbia, a 60-ton Right Whale materializes on top of someone's house and makes a big mess. The Foundation swoops in and covers the whole thing up. Not a big deal. Shit like this happens every day in the Foundation-verse.

Then some hikers find the remains of another whale impaled on a tree. Now the Foundation's is interested. They establish a task force to look for more dead whales in the Canadian back-country, and end up finding (literal) tons of them in various stages of decomposition. Dead whales in the treetops. Dead whales 300 kilometers inland. Dead whales embedded in the ground, or dashed out on rocks, or totally pureed as if they've been dropped from a great height. They do some cursory biological / genetic analysis on the remains. Turns out that they all come from a specific part of the Bering Sea.

Through means that I have yet to think up, the Foundation learns that the whales were teleported into the woods by poachers with anomalous hunting technology. Their intent was to beam the poor animals to a "chop shop" in the States, where they could be dissected and sold for oil and ambergris. Because their teleporters were faulty over long distances, only about 30% of the whales made it to the chop shop. The rest were randomly dispersed in the space between. When the poachers were confronted by a police patrol boat, they tried to teleport themselves the hell out of Dodge and met the same grisly fate as the other 70%.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a narrative mystery, with enough inherent wackiness to make it compelling.

SCP-XXXX refers to an inhabited region consisting of a small town and outlying farmland, located inland of the Transatlantic Mountains, south of the Ross Ice Shelf. Residents of SCP-XXXX refer to it as "Shackleton County." SCP-XXXX's fields can be seen to contain plants, resembling typical crops, in tilled snow, through unknown means. Residents of SCP-XXXX do not seem to suffer from discomfort or serious harm in the their cold environment, even without specialized clothing, but appear and behave typically in all other respects. Residents have been observed to use vehicles resembling large, closed-cabin snowmobiles comparable to personal automobiles and freight trucks. Residents are observed to leave the area of the "county" only once each month, when an organized group of 50-100 residents form a convoy, identifying their destination as "Erebus City." These departures are always accompanied by a blizzard causing near-total loss of visibility for Foundation observers, and attempts to track their location by other means have always failed to date. These convoys invariably return four days after their departure, similarly obscured, carrying personal and commercial goods. It is unknown where or how these items are obtained.

Central Narrative:
Central Narrative:

Containment of SCP-XXX relies heavily on Foundation sites disguised as research bases. In particular, sites on the Ross shelf are considered to be critical to the goal of maintaining containment without alerting SCP-XXXX's residents to containment efforts. Citing fears that such sites might be rendered unusable in the future if climate change causes the ice shelf to recede, a senior researcher proposes a plan under which the Foundation would become actively involved in fighting climate change. This proposal is rejected on the grounds that climate change is an element of consensus reality, and the potential threat to SCP-XXXX's containment is distant and insufficient to justify action. Convinced of the necessity of Foundation involvement in the issue, she seeks to undermine the consensus status of climate change by spreading memetic agents through public channels. While unsuccessful in creating the circumstances for Foundation intervention, this contributes to the popularity of denial movements regarding climate change, as well as dangerous containment breaches.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The use of a classic horror setting - Antarctic mountains - for a mostly-normal settlement, and the idea of a Foundation employee trying to force the Foundation into action outside its norms

Additional Notes: Honestly, this could easily become too polemical or goofy. I think it's a good basis, though.

item.description: Meteorites that reproduce like sea turtles.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Elevator Pitch:

  • Extraterrestrial animals that fly through space with telekinesis, feeding on planetary ring systems and other space debris and adding the matter to their rocky shells.
  • Look like rocks with organs inside, like Pyura chilensis. Could even use that animal for the picture, possibly.
  • Possibly silicon-based and composed entirely of biological rocks, if that's semi-plausible.
  • Reproduce through parthenogenesis, since they rarely cross paths in space. When ready to reproduce, they fall back to the planet of their birth, burning up in the atmosphere but leaving behind several metallic eggs in the crater.
  • After hatching, the babies consume some of the rocks in the area to build their shells before returning to space.

Central Narrative: The Containment Procedures involve traveling to locations of meteorite impacts to ensure that no civilians find any eggs, monitoring of asteroids to identify possible instances and predict their impact times and locations, and preventing NASA from detecting them. The description provides information on their biology and behavior. There's an addendum at the end chronicling observations of some captive instances and an experiment to see how they do in a non-space environment with gravity. No big twist.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is one of those strange, but not really dangerous, anomalies that does a good job of conveying the weirdness and wonder of the SCPverse without being horrific or grimdark. It's also kind of cute, I guess.

Additional Notes: Do I need to make them more dangerous? If so, I can just make it so the mother survives the impact and grows larger each time, meaning that her periodic returns to the same planet cause increasingly worse disasters at regular intervals. Then the procedures would involve destroying any recovered eggs, and possibly destroying any particularly large instances likely to return to Earth in the near future. I'd really rather leave them as quirky, strange, and kinda cute things that aren't especially dangerous or horrifying, though.

- Dr Vasiliev finds a radio and hears voices in the static that tell him there can be no more than ten, after which he tells everyone to gather in the cafeteria
- Dr Vasiliev counts 11 people and reluctantly notifies them that one of them has to die to stop the entity

Elevator Pitch: What happens when you put a space in between the past, and the present? This is the basis of Liminal spaces and what this SCP is based on. So what happens when you put someone in a dimension of nothing but liminal spaces? How would they affect someone and what if they could spread if they weren't monitored?

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this SCP to show liminal spaces activate memories and experiences we have never had, SCP-XXXX is a rotting wooden door attached to a concrete floor and concrete wall that has been ripped out of its original place, the inside being bigger than it's exterior. The inside contains a series of endless hallways with wooden doors lining each wall that lead deeper into SCP-XXXX with entryways to the next hallway every 10 miles. Each door that has never been unopened before leads to a completely random room correlating to the subject's suppressed memories, intentions, and or emotions, often being broken in ways like repeating sections or missing areas entirely, or random items in said rooms. The door must always stay closed for it is opened and consistently stayed open for longer than 20 minutes, the warped reality will spread to everything, including organic matter, concrete is found to be the least affected by this property. Exposure longer than 4 hours leads to a steady loss of direction.

+ show block
– hide block

So, what happens when someone is put inside for long periods of time? This is about a D class being put into SCP-XXXX for longer than a week. This leads to the D class to end up remembering who he is, his real name, and just why he was put on death row and forced to be a test subject in the foundation. This leads to acceptance of his actions, knowing that the foundation will mostly cut him off for retaining this information, he must come to terms knowing that he will either never make it out of here, or be killed by the foundation.

This SCP takes this idea of Liminal Spaces and turns it into an endless expanse of repeating rooms and endless, useless mazes of warped reality and turns it into an eerie dimension of random exploration.
